title: The clopen idempotent and the cut integral
statement:
Use the base $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, finite coefficient ring $A$ and geometric schemes of [sk-d-setup], the ordinary pro-etale derived categories $D(-,A)$ and the operations of [sk-d-six]. Let $E$ be a scheme proper over $s$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $j_B:B\hookrightarrow E$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] whose image is closed in $E$, and let $j_V:V\hookrightarrow E$ be the open immersion of the complementary open subscheme on $E\setminus j_B(B)$. Let

$$
e_B:A_E\xrightarrow{\eta_{j_B}}Rj_{B*}j_B^*A_E\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j_{B!}j_B^*A_E\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{j_B}}A_E
$$

be the composite of the unit of the ordinary adjunction $j_B^*\dashv Rj_{B*}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the inverse of the canonical comparison $j_{B!}\simeq Rj_{B*}$ induced termwise by the sheaf comparison $j_{B!}\to j_{B*}$ of [def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek-to-lower-star] (an isomorphism by [sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek]), for the open immersion $j_B$, which is also a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and hence proper ([lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]), and the counit of the extension-by-zero adjunction $j_{B!}\dashv j_B^*$ of [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions], i.e. the termwise sheaf counit of [def-weil-open-closed-recollement], with $j_{B!}$ the extension by zero of [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Then:

1. $e_B\circ e_B=e_B$ in $\operatorname{End}_{D(E,A)}(A_E)$.
2. Under the constant-coefficient identifications $j_B^*A_E\simeq A_B$ and $j_V^*A_E\simeq A_V$, one has $j_B^*e_B=\operatorname{id}_{A_B}$ and $j_V^*e_B=0$.
3. $B$ and $V$ are proper over $s$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and for every morphism $\alpha:A_E\to\omega_{E,A}$ in $D(E,A)$, where $\omega_{E,A}$ is the dualizing complex of [def-trf-dualizing-complex],
$$
\int_E(\alpha\circ e_B)=\int_B\alpha|_B\in A,
$$
where $\int_E,\int_B$ are the integrations of [def-trf-integration] and $\alpha|_B:A_B\to\omega_{B,A}$ is the restricted section of [def-trf-local-term] (constant pullback, $j_B^*\alpha$, open purity and dualizing composition). In particular the integral is $0$ when $B=\emptyset$ and is $\int_E\alpha$ when $B=E$.

source.place: node sk-d-local-term, order 2679: 'cuts out an idempotent' and 'which is $\int_B\alpha|_B$'; the argument is that of sk-p-local.proof.md (matrix of ordinary units and exceptional counits) specialized to the two-piece partition $E=B\sqcup V$

proof.text: Identify $B$ with its open image using [def-weil-open-immersion]. Since the image is closed, the map of structure sheaves $\mathcal O_E\to j_{B*}\mathcal O_B$ is surjective: on the open cover $B,V$ it is respectively the identity and the map to zero. Thus $j_B$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For $j_V$ the image is closed because $B$ is open, and $\mathcal O_E\to j_{V*}\mathcal O_V$ restricts to the identity on $V$ and the map to zero on $B$; hence $j_V$ is a closed immersion too. The two properness assertions follow from [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], part (b), applied to $E\to s$. In particular $B,V$ are separated finite type over $s$, and $E=B\sqcup V$ is the required finite clopen partition.

source.place: First paragraph: ordinary units and exceptional/open counits for a clopen partition; specialized to E=B disjoint union V

proof.text: Write $L=j_B^*$, $F=j_{B!}$ and $G=Rj_{B*}$. On module sheaves the canonical comparison $c:j_{B!}\to j_{B*}$ is an isomorphism by [sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek], using the compactification $(j_B,\operatorname{id}_E)$ and the properness just proved. Extension by zero here is the module extension of [def-weil-extension-by-zero]: in modules the left Kan extension is the direct sum over factorizations, of which there is at most one. Thus the exactness in [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] also makes $j_{B*}$ exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] they descend termwise; [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identifies this descent with the ordinary derived functor, via its canonical resolution map. The formula of [def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek-to-lower-star] consequently gives the derived comparison $c:F\to G$. This is exactly the termwise comparison whose inverse occurs in the statement, so it requires no identification with an unspecified compactification comparison. Write $\eta:\operatorname{id}\to GL$ and $v:LG\to\operatorname{id}$ for the ordinary unit and counit from [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and $u:\operatorname{id}\to LF$, $\varepsilon:FL\to\operatorname{id}$ for the open adjunction from [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]. Here $u$ is invertible; $v$ is invertible because $j_B$ is closed.

source.place: First paragraph: ordinary units and exceptional/open counits for a clopen partition; specialized to E=B disjoint union V

proof.text: First identify the derived counit $v$ with the termwise sheaf counit. By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] the adjunction $L\dashv G$ is the bijection of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], with $GM=Q(j_{B*}I(M))$ for the K-injective resolution $s:M\to I(M)$. Its characterizing formula, taken at the identity map and the identity quasi-isomorphism of $j_{B*}I(M)$, gives $v_M=Q(s)^{-1}\circ Q(\kappa_{I(M)})$, $\kappa$ the sheaf counit of $j_B^*\dashv j_{B*}$. Naturality of $\kappa$ along $s$ shows that under the isomorphism $Q(j_{B*}s):Q(j_{B*}M)\to GM$ (step 2: $j_{B*}$ is exact) $v_M$ is the termwise $Q(\kappa_M)$. Also $\varepsilon$ is termwise by [def-weil-open-closed-recollement]. Hence the termwise comparison of step 2 equals, in the derived category, the composite given by its defining expression, $c_M=\varepsilon_{GM}\circ F(v_M^{-1})$; compositions are written right to left. Its $L\dashv G$ adjunct is $v_M\circ Lc_M=u_M^{-1}$: indeed naturality of $u$ gives $LF(v_M^{-1})\circ u_M=u_{LGM}\circ v_M^{-1}$, and the triangle identity gives $L\varepsilon_{GM}\circ u_{LGM}=1$. Therefore $c_M=G(u_M^{-1})\circ\eta_{FM}$. Put $K=A_E$ and $r=c_{LK}^{-1}\circ\eta_K:K\to FLK$. The open triangle identity gives $L\varepsilon_K=u_{LK}^{-1}$, while naturality of $\eta$ gives $\eta_K\circ\varepsilon_K=GL(\varepsilon_K)\circ\eta_{FLK}$. Consequently $r\circ\varepsilon_K=c_{LK}^{-1}\circ G(u_{LK}^{-1})\circ\eta_{FLK}=1_{FLK}$. Since $e_B=\varepsilon_K\circ r$, one obtains $e_B^2=\varepsilon_K\circ(r\circ\varepsilon_K)\circ r=e_B$. These are identities of actual derived morphisms, not merely maps on cohomology.

source.place: First paragraph: ordinary units and exceptional/open counits for a clopen partition; specialized to E=B disjoint union V

proof.text: The identity $v_M\circ Lc_M=u_M^{-1}$ of step 3 gives $L(c_{LK}^{-1})=u_{LK}\circ v_{LK}$. Hence $Lr=u_{LK}\circ v_{LK}\circ L\eta_K=u_{LK}$ by the ordinary triangle identity. It follows that $Le_B=L\varepsilon_K\circ u_{LK}=1_{LK}=1_{A_B}$. On the other open, $j_V^*FLK=0$: in the defining extension-by-zero presheaf of [def-weil-extension-by-zero], every nonempty object over $V$ has no factorization through $B$, so its value is zero. At the empty object the sheaf axiom gives $M(\emptyset)=0$. Every member of every covering of such an object is still disjoint from $B$, so local sheafification also has zero value there. Thus extension by zero restricts to the zero sheaf on $V$, termwise also to the zero complex. The counit used in $e_B$ is the termwise sheaf counit by [def-weil-open-closed-recollement]; therefore $j_V^*e_B$ factors through zero and is zero. The constant pullback identifications are those already used in the statement.

source.place: First paragraph: ordinary units and exceptional/open counits for a clopen partition; specialized to E=B disjoint union V

proof.text: Set $\tau=\alpha\circ e_B$. Functoriality of pullback and the restriction formula in [def-trf-local-term] give $\tau|_B=\alpha|_B$ and $\tau|_V=0$, by step 4; the fixed open-purity and dualizing-composition isomorphisms are the same for $\tau$ and $\alpha$. Apply [lem-trf-integration-component-sum] to the two-piece partition $E=B\sqcup V$ from step 1. Its hypotheses hold: $E$ is separated finite type, and both pieces are proper. All dualizing objects and exceptional adjunctions are those of the geometric package in the statement, on their constructible domains. The two-summand formula yields $\int_E(\alpha\circ e_B)=\int_B\alpha|_B+\int_V0=\int_B\alpha|_B$, where the zero integral follows from [lem-trf-integration-linear]: apply it with the zero section for both arguments and scalar $-1$, then cancel to obtain $\int_V0=0$. No assertion that restriction detects arbitrary derived morphism equality is used.

source.place: First paragraph: ordinary units and exceptional/open counits for a clopen partition; specialized to E=B disjoint union V

proof.text: If $B=\emptyset$, then $j_{B!}=0$ directly from [def-weil-extension-by-zero]: an object over $E$ factors through $\emptyset$ only when it is empty, where every module sheaf has value $0$. Hence $e_B=0$ and $\int_E(\alpha\circ e_B)=\int_E0=0$ by [lem-trf-integration-linear], as in step 5. If $B=E$, i.e. $j_B$ is surjective, then $V=\emptyset$. Apply [lem-trf-integration-component-sum] to $\alpha$ itself and the partition $E=B\sqcup V$ of step 1: $\int_E\alpha=\int_B\alpha|_B+\int_V\alpha|_V$. The last term is $0$ by the empty case ($T=V=\emptyset$, empty index set) of the same lemma. With step 5, $\int_E(\alpha\circ e_B)=\int_B\alpha|_B=\int_E\alpha$. This does not identify $e_B$ with $1$, so it holds for every open immersion $j_B$ onto $E$, not only the identity, and it covers $E=\emptyset$.
